source_text: Ἐγέλα ποτὲ πλατὺν κατὰ τῆς ἀνθρωπίνης φύσεως ὁ διάβολος γέλωτα, καὶ ταῖς συμφοραῖς ἡμῶν ἑορταῖς ἐπευφραίνεται. Ἀλλ' ὁ μὲν γέλως τριήμερος· ὁ δὲ θρῆνος αἰώνιος· καὶ πλατὺς γέλως θρῆνον αὐτῷ πλατύτερον κατεσκεύασεν, δάκρυον ἀδιάλειπτον, κλαυθμὸν ἀπαρηγόρητον· βέλος ἐγκάρδιον. Τοῦτο τὸ βέλος ἐν τῇ παρθενικῇ καμίνῳ, οἷον ἠθέλησεν, καὶ ὡς ἠθέλησεν, διὰ πυρὸς κατὰ τοῦ ἐχθροῦ ὁ πολεμάρχης ἐχάλκευσεν· καὶ στομώσας τῇ ἐνεργείᾳ τῆς ἀηττήτου θεότητος, καὶ βάψας τῷ ὕδατι τοῦ ἀχράντου βαπτίσματος, καὶ ἀκονήσας τοῖς ἀπαθέσι παθήμασιν, καὶ στιλβώσας διὰ τῆς μυστικῆς ἀναστάσεως· δι' ἑαυτοῦ πανστρατιᾷ τὸν ἀλάστορα ἐθανάτωσε. Ποῖος οὖν λόγος ἢ τὴν ἡμετέραν χαρὰν ἢ τὴν ἐκείνου συμφορὰν διηγήσηται; Ὁ γὰρ ποτὲ ἀρχάγγελος, νῦν διάβολος· ὁ ποτὲ ἐν οὐρανοῖς διαιτώμενος, νῦν ὡς ὄφις ἐπὶ γῆς θεωρεῖται συρόμενος· ὁ ποτὲ μετὰ τῶν χερουβὶμ ἀγαλλόμενος, νῦν ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ τῶν χοίρων ἐγκέκλεισται ὀδυνόμενος· ὅνπερ τροπωσόμεθα ἐναντία τῆς ἐκείνου φρονήσαντες προαιρέσεως· χάριτι καὶ φιλανθρωπίᾳ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ· ᾧ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, Ἀμήν.
thought_title: The devil's short laughter and endless grief
orientation: The devil's laughter at human misfortune lasted three days, but his grief is endless. Christ forged in the Virgin's womb the arrow that killed him, and the fallen archangel now crawls like a snake. The sermon ends by calling the hearers to rout him by choosing the opposite of what he chose, and closes with a doxology.
pass_a_gloss: Once the devil laughed a broad laugh against human nature, and over our misfortunes as festivals rejoices. But the laughter [was] three-day, but the lament eternal; and broad laughter prepared for him a broader lament, an unceasing tear, an inconsolable weeping; an in-the-heart arrow. This arrow in the virginal furnace, such as he willed and as he willed, through fire against the enemy the war-leader forged; and having given it an edge/hardened by the working of the unconquered Godhead, and having dipped/tempered [it] in the water of the undefiled baptism, and having whetted [it] with the passionless sufferings, and having polished [it] through the mystical resurrection; through himself with full army/force he put to death the avenging spirit/destroyer. What word then will recount either our joy or that one's calamity? For he once archangel, now devil; he once living in the heavens, now as a snake on earth is seen being dragged/crawling; he once exulting with the cherubim, now in the keeping/prison of the swine has been shut up, suffering pain; whom we shall rout, having set our minds on things opposite to his choice; by the grace and love for mankind of our Lord Jesus Christ; to whom [be] the glory and the might to the ages of the ages, Amen.

pass_b_english: Once the devil laughed a broad laugh at human nature, and made merry over our misfortunes as though they were feasts. But his laughter lasted three days, while his lament is everlasting. The broad laughter prepared for him a broader lament: tears that never stop, weeping that finds no comfort, an arrow in the heart.

The Commander forged this arrow by fire against the enemy in the furnace of the Virgin, of such a kind as He willed and in the way He willed. He hardened its edge by the working of the unconquerable Godhead, tempered it in the water of the spotless baptism, sharpened it on the sufferings that knew no passion, and polished it through the mystical resurrection. Then by Himself, with His whole force, He put the accursed one to death.

What words, then, could describe either our joy or his calamity? For he who was once an archangel is now a devil. He who once lived in the heavens is now seen crawling on the earth like a snake (Genesis 3:14). He who once exulted with the cherubim is now shut up in the pen of the swine, in anguish. We shall rout him by setting our minds on the opposite of what he chose, through the grace and love for mankind of our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom be glory and might for ever and ever. Amen.
notes: 'Crawling on the earth like a snake' alludes to the curse on the serpent, Genesis 3:14.
'His laughter lasted three days' refers to the three days of Christ's death and burial; no single verse is cited.
'Furnace of the Virgin' (ἐν τῇ παρθενικῇ καμίνῳ) means the womb of the Virgin, where the Commander (πολέμαρχος, 'war-leader') forged the arrow, that is, the Incarnation.
The smith's sequence is kept: στομόω 'harden the edge', βάπτω 'dip' (the quench-tempering of steel, with a play on βάπτισμα 'baptism'), ἀκονάω 'whet', στιλβόω 'polish'.
ἀπαθέσι παθήμασιν is a deliberate paradox ('passionless sufferings'), rendered 'the sufferings that knew no passion'.
πανστρατιᾷ ('with the whole army, in full force') is joined with δι' ἑαυτοῦ ('by himself'): Christ alone acts as a whole army; rendered 'by Himself, with His whole force'.
ἀλάστωρ ('avenging spirit; accursed wretch' in LSJ; used of the devil in Lampe) is rendered 'the accursed one'.
τροπωσόμεθα is rendered 'rout' to match τροποῦται ('is routed') in the previous section; φιλανθρωπία in the doxology is rendered 'love for mankind', matching 'Lover of mankind' there.

ἐπευφραίνεται is present tense in a past narrative and is rendered in the past for clarity. θρῆνον ... πλατύτερον pairs a masculine noun with a neuter-looking comparative, as printed; the sense is clear ('a broader lament').

φυλακή τῶν χοίρων is rendered 'the pen of the swine'; φυλακή may also mean 'prison' (compare Revelation 20:7). The allusion to the swine of Matthew 8:30-32 and Mark 5:11-13 is possible, not certain, and is left uncited.

Other allusions left uncited as uncertain: the fall from heaven (Luke 10:18; Isaiah 14:12) and exulting with the cherubim (Ezekiel 28:14). The closing doxology is a liturgical formula and is not cited.
Capitalised pronouns (He, His, Himself) mark Christ; lowercase pronouns mark the devil.
